sections.heading: Red Light Tickets in El Paso Are an Officer's Word, Not a Camera's
paragraphs: If you got a red light ticket in El Paso, it was handed to you by a police officer, a deputy or a trooper — not mailed from a camera. Texas outlawed red-light cameras statewide in 2019, and El Paso has none. A camera ticket comes with a timestamped photo; an officer-issued ticket comes with one person's memory of a moment that lasted under a second, usually viewed from a cruiser parked at an angle to the intersection.

The typical citation reads "disregard traffic control device" or "ran red light." The officer must have seen the light turn red before your front tires crossed the stop line. From a side street or a position behind you, the officer often cannot see both the signal face and your bumper at the same time. That gap between what was seen and what has to be proved is where these cases are contested.

Paying the ticket is a guilty plea: a moving-violation conviction on your DPS record that insurers can see at renewal. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but DPS may suspend the license of a "habitual violator" — four or more moving-violation convictions arising from separate incidents within 12 consecutive months, or seven or more within 24 months (Transp. Code §521.292(b)). This page is general information, not legal advice about your case — but don't pay it before you've had it reviewed.

sections.heading: Rolling Stops and Stop Sign Tickets
paragraphs: A stop sign ticket is usually a "rolling stop" — the officer says you slowed but never fully stopped. Texas requires a complete stop, and the difference between 2 mph and 0 mph is something an officer estimates by eye, often from well down the block. In neighborhoods off Mesa Street on the West Side or along the residential grids near Hanks and Eastwood, these tickets are written in batches during enforcement details.

The defense questions are specific. Where exactly was the officer? Was the view of your wheels blocked by a parked car, a fence or a hedge? Was the sign itself visible, or faded, bent or hidden by a tree? We photograph the intersection, pull the officer's notes and present the problems to the prosecutor at the pretrial docket.

sections.heading: Why Vantage Point and Signal Timing Decide These Cases
paragraphs: Two facts matter more than anything else in a red light case: where the officer was, and how long the yellow lasted. Big El Paso intersections like Mesa and Resler, Montana and Yarbrough, or Zaragoza and Pellicano have multiple signal heads, long crossing distances and heavy turning traffic. An officer sitting on the cross street sees their own light turn green and infers that yours turned red — but a protected left-turn phase or an all-red clearance interval can mean your signal was still yellow when you entered.

Yellow timing is the other lever. Yellow intervals are set according to the approach speed, and a yellow that is short for a 45 mph road leaves drivers in a "dilemma zone" where they can neither stop safely nor clear the intersection before red. That is a legitimate issue to raise with the prosecutor, and it is why we ask every client exactly which lane and direction they were traveling.

sections.heading: From Notice of Appearance to Pretrial Docket
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance right away, which stops the appearance date from becoming a failure-to-appear warrant. We review the citation for defects, check whether the officer is still with the department, and build the vantage-point questions described above.

At the pretrial docket we negotiate for the best available result given the citation, your record and the court. In El Paso Municipal Court that is often a deferred disposition: a court fee, a violation-free deferral period, and a dismissal with no conviction. For drivers who qualify, a defensive driving dismissal is another route. When the officer's position was genuinely poor or the officer can't appear, we press for an outright dismissal. You generally do not need to attend. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Write It Down Tonight, Then Send It to Us
paragraphs: While it's fresh, write down the details: direction, lane, where the officer's vehicle was, time of day and weather. If you can safely do it, photograph the intersection from your approach showing the signal heads or the stop sign. These details fade in a week and they are exactly what we use.

Then check the appearance date and do not let it pass, and do not request defensive driving on your own, which can lock you into a plea. If the date already passed, there is probably a warrant — go to our warrant recall page or use the free ticket and warrant lookup, and call us the same day. When you hire us, send the citation (both sides), your driver's license, your insurance card, your written notes and photos of the intersection, and any mail the court has already sent.

faqs.q: Does El Paso have red light cameras?
faqs.a: No. Texas banned red-light cameras statewide in 2019, and El Paso has none. Every red light ticket here is written by an officer who personally observed the intersection, so the case rests on that officer's vantage point and testimony rather than a photograph.

faqs.q: Is a rolling stop really a ticket?
faqs.a: Yes. Texas requires a complete stop, and officers write "rolling stop" tickets regularly in El Paso neighborhoods. Whether you actually stopped, and whether the officer could see your wheels from where they were parked, is exactly what we challenge.

faqs.q: What if the light was yellow when I entered the intersection?
faqs.a: Then you did not run a red light. The violation is entering the intersection after the signal turns red; being inside it when the light changes is lawful. A protected turn arrow or a short yellow often explains what the officer thought they saw.

faqs.q: Will a red light ticket raise my insurance?
faqs.a: If you pay it, it becomes a moving-violation conviction on your Texas driving record, and a conviction may affect premiums depending on your history, carrier and other rating factors. A dismissal or deferred disposition keeps the conviction off the record so there is nothing for your insurer to rate.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court?
faqs.a: Generally not for a red light or stop sign ticket in El Paso County. We appear on your behalf, negotiate at the pretrial docket and report the result. A trial is uncommon, and we would discuss it with you first.

faqs.q: I was ticketed at a stop sign in Horizon City. Can you handle that?
faqs.a: Yes. We handle red light and stop sign tickets in El Paso Municipal Court, every El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct, and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony municipal courts. Our flat fee in those courts is $69 per ticket.
